props.gloss_en: whoever enjoys a groom's feast and does not gladden him transgresses five voices
the source: 'the voice of joy and the voice of gladness, the voice of the groom and the voice of the bride, the voice of those who say: give thanks to the Lord of hosts' (Jer 33:11)
if he gladdens him, his reward: he merits the Torah
the Torah was given with five voices

the source: 'and it was on the third day, when it was morning, there were sounds and lightning and a thick cloud upon the mountain, and the voice of the shofar...; and the voice of the shofar... and God answered him by a voice' (Ex 19:16, 19)
but it is written: 'and all the people saw the voices' (Ex 20:15) -- further voices at Sinai
R' Abbahu: [one who gladdens the groom] is as if he offered a thanks-offering
the source: 'those who bring a thanks-offering to the house of the Lord' (Jer 33:11)
Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak: [one who gladdens the groom] is as if he rebuilt one of Jerusalem's ruins
the source: 'for I will restore the captivity of the land as at first, says the Lord' (Jer 33:11)
